speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In the biomedical sciences sector for example, the nascent field of Precision Medicine has strong growth potential, with a global market size of US$74 billion in 2022, which is expected to grow at an average rate of 11.5% a year up to 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will identify and nurture potential promising local startups, with the potential to develop cutting-edge solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One such company, Engine Biosciences, has developed a proprietary platform which uses AI, machine learning and gene editing to discover gene interactions to yield promising new therapies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Engine Biosciences is currently in the pre-clinical stage and intends to leverage its R&D base in Singapore to expand into the international market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must stay abreast of these developments and ensure that our businesses can reap the AI dividend.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We hope that each of these companies will become a Centre of Excellence (CoE) for AI in its own right.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also set up sectoral AI CoEs to address sector-wide use cases and build domain-specific capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a start, A*STAR will launch a manufacturing sector AI CoE by the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The CoE will convene stakeholders from industry, research and the startup scene to develop AI-enabled solutions that addresses use cases in the manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will learn from this pilot and study how we might expand the same thing to the other sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The transition to a low-carbon and sustainable economy will also present new green growth opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For instance, we have established a vibrant carbon services and trading ecosystem to take advantage of the growth in the global carbon market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are also opportunities to develop sustainable products, such as biofuels, Sustainable Aviation Fuel and green chemicals, which support our green growth objectives.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, Neste expanded its biorefinery in Singapore in 2023, making us the world's largest producer of Sustainable Aviation Fuel.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, chemicals company Arkema has built its bio-factory on Jurong Island to produce high-performance polymers made from sustainable materials.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are also working closely with the marine and offshore engineering (M&OE) sector to ensure that it is productive, globally competitive and well-positioned to leverage new growth opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This requires the sector to rethink its operating model, pivot to higher-skilled, higher-value activities and reduce its reliance on foreign manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will monitor developments in the sector before making further adjustments.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also proceed with the increase in foreign worker levies announced in 2013, but deferred in view of the M&OE downturn and COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These moves will be discussed further in MOM's COS segment, as part of the Government's broader manpower strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will enable us to become a globally impactful and thriving hub that can deliver sustainable solutions in an M&OE value chain.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some companies have already embarked on this journey, such as Seatrium, which is working on several large offshore wind projects.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will identify and capture opportunities along the value chain and anchor them in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One promising local startup is BeeX, which designs, builds and deploys hovering autonomous underwater vehicles (HAUVs) to conduct inspections of offshore windfarms.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: BeeX built its first HAUV with a $500,000 Startup SG Tech grant.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Its solutions have been validated internationally and it is currently working on a high-specification, second-generation HAUV+.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I have outlined our plans to continue attracting quality investments into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also support enterprise collaborations and invest in our innovation ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Mark Lee and Mr Edward Chia will be happy to know that we will enhance the Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme, or PACT scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, the scheme encourages partnerships between larger and smaller enterprises, between MNCs, large local enterprises (LLEs) and the SMEs, on supplier development and co-innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Going forward, we will expand PACT to more industries and modalities, including capability training, internationalisation and corporate venturing.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Allow me to share a few examples of collaborations facilitated by PACT.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: GlobalFoundries was able to work closely with its supplier, Forefront AM, to scale up its capability in additive manufacturing, so that it can repair some of GlobalFoundries' high-value semiconductor manufacturing tools.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another example is SATS, which has organised capacity building workshops with PACT support, to help its SME suppliers understand and track their carbon emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will provide more opportunities for SMEs to level up their capabilities, enhance their competitiveness and plug into global and regional value chains.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also invest in innovation efforts, including upstream research, translation and commercialisation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Since its launch in 2016, the Startup SG Equity Scheme has catalysed over $2.3 billion in private-sector funding for over 230 Singapore-based startups, including in new growth areas, such as advanced manufacturing, pharmaceuticals and biologics or pharmbio, medical technology or medtech, and agriculture-food technology or agri-food tech.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And we are working on further enhancements to the Startup SG Equity Scheme and will announce details later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, while we will need to continue tapping on global talent to complement our local workforce to grow our economy, we will redouble our efforts to strengthen our local talent pool, so that Singaporeans can benefit from this growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And at the same time we need to invest in our longer-term future and drive economic growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We can achieve this by leveraging our trade networks, spearheading the adoption of new technologies and developing our talent.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Economic transformation has always been a key priority for us.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng earlier underlined the importance of transformation in our growth journey.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Indeed, transformation is the constant in this fast-changing world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must remain agile and continue to grow our economy by seizing new opportunities, making ourselves ever more productive, innovative and competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While there will still be uncertainties and challenges in the future, if all of us work together as Team Singapore – with workers, businesses, trade associations and chambers and unions each playing our part, we can remain relevant on the global stage and enhance our heft.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We can seize new opportunities for growth, improve the lives of all Singaporeans and build our shared future together.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore is a small nation with limited resource endowments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Despite so, we have grown to become a leading global city that we are today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But to sustain this growth, we will need to maximise our resource potential and turn these potentials into the next bound of success.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: My speech today would touch on how we can continue to push boundaries, to unlock our resource potential and to bring in new opportunities in four areas: first, energy and carbon; second, research and development; third, manpower; and last but not least, land.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Climate change poses an asymmetric, long-term challenge to all countries across the globe.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As a low-lying island-state, Singapore is disproportionately impacted by climate change.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our resource constraints are more stark compared to many other countries, which makes decarbonisation even more challenging.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But even so, we firmly believe that Singapore can rise above these constraints and achieve and thrive in a net-zero future.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Today, I will share more about our efforts to invest in new decarbonisation pathways, while ensuring a stable power system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First and foremost, a stable electricity market along with a reliable and secure power system must be the foundation upon which we advance Singapore's energy transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Alongside a stable electricity market, we need a reliable grid.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Edward Chia asked whether our power grid is robust enough to integrate diverse energy sources.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: While largely fueled by natural gas, our grid today already takes in other energy sources, such as solar power and waste-to-energy, while maintaining high grid reliability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Over the next few decades, we expect more diverse energy sources to enter our grid and we are upgrading our grid management systems in preparation for this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Looking ahead, we expect electricity demand to grow with increasing digitalisation, economic growth and electrification, as Mr Edward Chia mentioned.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: EMA works closely with agencies to ensure that we have sufficient capacity to meet this demand.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: That is why we have launched tenders for new generation capacity in the form of greener and more energy-efficient power plants.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: EMA recently awarded YTL Power Seraya the right to build, own and operate a Combined Cycle Gas Turbine (CCGT).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This CCGT will have a carbon intensity 10% lower than that of existing CCGTs in the system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It will be the third CCGT to be built that can run on hydrogen, which is a potential low-carbon fuel and will be up by 2028.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is in addition to Keppel's and Sembcorp's hydrogen-ready plants which are currently under construction.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singapore's energy transition will be a multi-decade journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the meantime, natural gas will still play an important role over the next one to two decades.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: SLNG is, therefore, developing a second Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) terminal to meet our gas needs and to strengthen our energy security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: While natural gas is the cleanest fossil fuel, we have to green our power supplies if we want to achieve our net-zero commitments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are working on realising low-carbon electricity import projects and studying low-carbon energy alternatives, such as hydrogen and ammonia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Jessica Tan would be glad to know that we have made good progress.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To Mr Edward Chia's question, we are on track to achieve this target.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Companies are currently conducting feasibility studies and securing regulatory approvals from source and transit countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: When realised, these projects will also form the building blocks of an ASEAN Power Grid.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also studying the potential of various other low-carbon energy sources.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For hydrogen, we will start with a small-scale pathfinder project to test and to deploy a direct ammonia combustion power plant, alongside ammonia bunkering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Request for Proposal (RFP) to select a lead developer for this project is ongoing and we will close this later this month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Geothermal is another potential energy source that we are studying.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will be conducting a nationwide non-invasive geophysical study to assess Singapore's deep geothermal resource potential for power generation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: EMA is evaluating the RFP proposals and we will also announce the award soon.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Advanced nuclear energy technologies and fusion energy are also potential game-changers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We engage international organisations widely and countries with deep capabilities in nuclear energy to broaden our understanding of advanced nuclear energy technologies, including Small Modular Reactors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is so that we can assess the suitability of these technologies for Singapore, once they are proven to be safe and viable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan spoke about the potential of the energy from the sun – fusion energy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: While there have been significant breakthroughs in the fusion energy space in recent years, there still remain engineering challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond the fact that there are no demonstrator plants today that can generate electricity, there are also other challenges, including the low global supply of tritium, which is an important fuel for fusion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As such, there is a big difference in opinions among experts on when fusion can be commercialised safely.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also keeping a close watch on the development of fusion energy and we are collaborating with overseas research entities to build up capabilities in this field.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue to identify capabilities in our local ecosystem that are fusion-relevant and where we could potentially play a role in the fusion supply chain.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At the same time, R&D investments, such as those under the Low Carbon Energy Research, or LCER Programme, can help us realise the potential of low-carbon alternatives and support efforts to expand the range of technological solutions suited for Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These projects collectively seek to address key challenges that Singapore faces in deploying hydrogen in areas, such as energy efficiency, durability and safety.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond hydrogen, we also want to support research into emerging technologies with the potential to sprout into needle moving solutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Lastly, our close relationships with International Organisations help us to build capabilities to accelerate energy transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This Centre is the IEA's first office outside of its headquarters in Paris and is also Singapore's first energy-focused international organisation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Centre will provide technical advice and policy support to governments and regional bodies to accelerate the energy transition, for example, through scaling up the deployment of renewable energy and other clean energy technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We expect the Centre to be operational by the end of this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members, I have spoken at length on our plans to transition and decarbonise our power sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Despite our lack of indigenous renewable energy resources, Singapore must still embark on the energy transition to stay relevant in a world that is moving towards net-zero.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I am glad that several businesses are already pioneering such clean energy projects, as Mr Mark Lee pointed out earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But to decarbonise, we will need to deploy clean energy at scale.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will likely involve nascent technologies, come with significant commercial and geopolitical risks, or require high upfront capital expenditures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: All these would require substantial investment from governments and companies alike.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In instances where projects are of strategic value to Singapore's decarbonisation journey, the Government will provide support to catalyse the development of such projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will help Singapore secure reliable and cleaner energy supply, at the scale and speed required to meet our climate goals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is with this in mind that the Government will set up the new Future Energy Fund, as announced by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Fund can support the infrastructure investments we need to deploy low-carbon technologies, such as for hydrogen, when they are viable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Edward Chia asked if we would need to top up the Fund further.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will do so when our fiscal space allows for it and depending on our development plans for the energy transition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The path ahead is not straightforward and we will need to adapt and be nimble when circumstances change.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But rest assured that the Government will take great care in charting our energy transition, to ensure that even as we decarbonise, we maintain our energy security and we will remain cost-competitive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In particular, we are mindful of the potential impact of energy transition on electricity prices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also continue supporting our lower- and middle-income households to mitigate the impact that the transition will have on electricity costs and we will continue helping our businesses reduce energy consumption, improve energy efficiency and, in turn, lower their energy costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members, other than the power sector, our industrial processes also contribute a significant portion of Singapore's emissions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will need to actively pursue pathways to decarbonise our industrial processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As mentioned by Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean in Prime Minister's Office's COS, one such pathway we are developing is carbon capture and storage (CCS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: CCS involves the capture of emissions from point sources, such as chemical plants or power plants.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The carbon dioxide is then transported to suitable geological formations where they are injected and stored deep underground.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have been engaging companies interested to pursue CCS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government will work with S Hub to evaluate the techno-economic feasibility of aggregating emissions from Singapore and collaborate with regional partners to study potential carbon dioxide storage sites.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are keen to work with like-minded partners to make cross-border CCS projects a reality and realise the potential of our entire region as a CCS hub.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Under the LOI, both countries will set up a workgroup to advance CCS cooperation between Singapore and Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Continued investment in R&D is critical in ensuring that we maintain our edge and competitiveness in other areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To Ms Jessica Tan's, Mr Shawn Huang's and Mr Neil Parekh's questions, MTI will double down on our efforts to support R&D investments, particularly in deep tech R&D for critical and novel technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Deep tech typically requires a long development in commercialisation period due to the extent of tech validation and the risks involved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Investments in deep tech would enable us to entrench R&D that diversifies our economy by growing new industry clusters, thereby generating new economic opportunities for Singapore, propelling us towards innovation-led growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are creating new R&D translation platforms and providing additional resourcing to catalyse four key sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Semiconductor is a sector with significant barriers to entry due to high investment costs, with clean rooms and machines that can cost millions of dollars.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: NSTIC aims to help companies and researchers overcome this by providing them access to semiconductor infrastructure and supporting prototyping and small volume manufacturing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I recently visited MetaOptics Technologies, a local startup that designs and fabricates flat lens and optical devices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These flat lenses are hundred of times thinner than a human hair, allowing for size reduction for devices like optical sensors and cameras.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MetaOptics intends to leverage NSTIC's research expertise and fabrication services to make devices locally, instead of having to outsource to overseas foundries which have higher costs and longer turnaround times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MetaOptics is also being supported by two scientists seconded to the company from A*STAR, through its Technology for Enterprise Capability Upgrading Programme (T-Up), which Mr Desmond Choo asked about earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, A*STAR has launched a $97-million Nucleic Acid Therapeutics Initiative (NATi) to position Singapore as the regional node for research, clinical translation and commercialisation of RNA drugs and vaccines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Most of us would have heard about RNA vaccines during COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singapore has actually been developing capabilities in RNA research over the years through sustained investments in biomedical research and development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Through NATi, Singapore will accelerate the development of RNA drugs and vaccines and grow our RNA manufacturing capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We currently have at least 10 local SMEs across the value chain for RNA therapeutics, and NATi will support and grow more local SMEs and startups and attract more companies here.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, A*STAR will launch MedTech Catapult – a $38 million initiative to accelerate the development of novel Life Science Tools and Medical Devices, by working with companies and product owners to translate research into commercial products.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This initiative will help intermediaries, like local contract manufacturing organisations, to move up the value chain so that they can not only manufacture but also develop their own MedTech product design and capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Through MedTech Catapult, we also aim to train and upskill product engineers who can then go on to serve in the industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Fourth, a new tranche of about $60 million funding will be provided to the National Robotics Programme (NRP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Started in 2016, the NRP has delivered good outcomes, such as the development of the Robotics Middleware Framework, which enables different brands of robots to work seamlessly with each other by standardising communications and de-conflicting navigation routes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Moving forward, the NRP will step up translation of our robotics research and development capabilities, particularly in sectors, such as manufacturing, logistics, facilities management and healthcare.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It will do this through “RoboClusters”, bringing together public sector researchers, end-users and robotics companies to foster collaborations and co-development of solutions with economic potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: NRP will also help to accelerate the growth of promising Singapore-based robotics SMEs and startups.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked how MTI will grow the talent pool in research and development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: All these will contribute to the development of an open and inclusive ecosystem where research, innovation and enterprise can come together to create commercially meaningful outcomes for businesses and help our industry partners to scale-up.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We need to strengthen our workforce competitiveness in tandem with our economic competitiveness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As Minister Gan shared earlier, we are committed to creating good opportunities for Singaporeans as we grow our economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To empower Singaporeans to seize these opportunities, our workforce will need to be equipped with the relevant skillsets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So stay tuned, I will share more details in my MOM COS speech on MOM's plans to support workers at all levels to enhance their employability, strengthen their career health and acquire overseas work experience; and how the Global Business Leaders Programme, as mentioned earlier by Minister Gan, will support Singaporean middle to senior managers with leadership potential to acquire the relevant overseas work experience and leadership skills to become corporate leaders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will complement the bilateral manpower programmes MTI is developing with Indonesia and Vietnam.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will support our companies and Singaporeans to tap on exciting opportunities in our fast-growing region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the Government's efforts in ensuring that we have sufficient land to meet our competing industrial, housing and recreational needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Ministry of National Development will share more on the Government's master-planning process and how we balance across competing land use needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In planning for industrial estates, the JTC Corporation seeks to optimise industrial land usage through land intensification and recycling, as well as the siting of industrial uses within mixed-use districts near to housing and recreational facilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our upcoming new industrial districts like Punggol Digital District (PDD) and Jurong Innovation District (JID) are designed to embody this philosophy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: PDD will house the new Singapore Institute of Technology campus alongside digital tech companies to create opportunities for applied learning and to build a robust pipeline of local technological talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: JID supports Singapore's Manufacturing 2030 ambition to become a global business, innovation and talent hub for advanced manufacturing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The anchoring of companies alongside A*STAR's Advanced Remanufacturing and Technology Centre (ARTC), which has collaborations with about 100 industry players – inclusive of Government agencies, research institutes and academia; will help to accelerate innovations to create an advanced manufacturing ecosystem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: JTC will also rejuvenate key industrial estates in Sungei Kadut, Ang Mo Kio and Kallang-Kolam Ayer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: JTC's tenants can look forward to smarter and more sustainable facilities and infrastructure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Suitable existing buildings and structures will also be identified for potential adaptive reuse and will serve as activity nodes for workers and the surrounding community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: More details will be provided within the Urban Redevelopment Authority's (URA's) Draft Master Plan 2025.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I spoke about how we would unlock potential in the areas of energy and carbon, research and development, land and manpower.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: That said, the path forward would not be easy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In fact, it has never been easy for a resource-constrained nation like Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But as the Chinese saying goes, "时势造英雄", which translates to "tough times create not just heroes, but also heroines".

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We were small, with no natural resource endowment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But together, our people managed to make it work, by carefully optimising whatever resources we have coupled with human ingenuity and innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With good planning and strong support from businesses and Singaporeans, I am confident we can and we will be able to unlock our resource potential to strive for the next bound of growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Only through this way, our businesses can continue to stay competitive, keep our edge and bring more opportunities and benefits to Singapore and Singaporeans for many more decades to come.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, the world we face today is vastly different from what it used to be.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Earlier, Minister Gan Kim Yong shared how the global uncertainties have strained our small and open economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Change, continual transformation and innovation form the present order of things.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To thrive in the new normal, we need a positive mindset to embrace transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, if you recall, during the COVID-19 pandemic, our businesses managed to overcome the resistance to change, including the heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our enterprises have shown the ability to transform to secure a better future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure all the Members that MTI and our economic agencies, the Government is committed to supporting our businesses' transformation journey for the long haul.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, I will elaborate on how the Government is ramping up critical support for companies to transform and thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As highlighted earlier by Mr Shawn Huang, we are determined to help businesses seize fresh opportunities in new growth areas, such as sustainability and digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I will also delve into how, for instance, we will drive sectoral transformation for the M&OE industry as mentioned by Minister Gan Kim Yong earlier; and continue the momentum of positive change in our heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I will also share how the Government will help accelerate the green transition of our Singapore enterprises to benefit and to future-proof our business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, I will touch on how we will help companies capture emerging digital opportunities for their next bound of growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These efforts cover strategic areas such as innovation, digitalisation, jobs and skills, internationalisation, productivity and sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many sectors have shown progress in their roadmap and we will not let up our efforts to support their transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The M&OE sector, as Minister Gan has mentioned earlier, is undergoing substantial changes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Mr Shawn Huang that this traditionally labour-intensive sector will need to transform to stay competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To this end, we aim to turbocharge the M&OE sector to capture emerging opportunities in areas, like offshore wind and maritime decarbonisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, several trailblazers in the sector have pivoted their businesses to serve in these growing markets that I mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One company that really stands out for raising their green capabilities is Penguin International.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Now, this is a homegrown shipbuilder, homegrown ship owner and one of the world's largest aluminium shipbuilders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Penguin International has spent the past few years future-proofing themselves, building up their in-house capabilities in designing, constructing and operating green vessels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Currently, the company is working with Shell to build and operate three electric ferries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These eco-friendly ferries are expected to cut carbon dioxide emissions by about 6,000 tonnes annually.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is comparable to the environmental impact of roughly 18,000 one-way road trips from Singapore to Bangkok.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: That is the impact of three electric ferries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides offering near-term transitional support for M&OE companies to fulfil their pre-committed contract deliveries, we will refresh the M&OE Industry Digital Plan to encourage greater adoption of sector-specific productivity-boosting digital solutions as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, new career opportunities are being identified.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will equip Singaporeans with fresh digital skills for higher-value work in the M&OE sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Furthermore, Workforce Singapore will expand its Career Conversion Programme to include offshore wind to develop local, mid-career talents for offshore wind farm development and operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Crucially, we will lay the foundation for a strong talent pipeline by nurturing interest in M&OE careers amongst our youth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTI will work closely with the industry and ASMI to enhance the sector's attractiveness and encourage more M&OE companies to offer industry scholarships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am glad that together with our agencies, ASMI has developed a new Industry Plan that sets out the strategies to enable the businesses to seize new green growth opportunities and get equipped for longer-term transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: ASMI will share their plans in the next few months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Shawn Huang they spoke very passionately about this topic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure them that our heartland enterprises are making good progress in digitalisation and retail innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, more than 17,000 heartland enterprises have adopted e-payment solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, more than 12,000 heartland enterprises now have online presence, about two-third.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Those who have embraced digital transformation have gained a bigger customer base, beyond their neighbourhoods, beyond footfall, to even online customers and some shops have even attracted overseas customers as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Bee Choo Origin, a hair product company that started in Ang Mo Kio as a hair salon in 2007, is a good example.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Its owner, Mdm Cheah Bee Chew, who began as a home-based hairdresser, grew her humble salon into a global hair treatment company.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It began selling its products online in 2020, again due to COVID-19, and then saw their revenue rise by 25% in just three years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, Bee Choo Origin has 170 stores spanning 11 markets and is entering its next lap of growth under the leadership of Mdm Cheah's 34-year-old daughter, Estee.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The retail sector is evolving rapidly, with the growth of technology, e-commerce and fast-changing consumer preferences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Alongside this, we also welcome the first batch of retailers under the Heartland Innovation and Transformation (HIT) Programme, or 创新在邻里计划, who will be unveiling their products in Ang Mo Kio.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am very heartened that some of these retailers from these new waves of shops have come up with concepts and innovative products for better health and well-being to meet the needs of the society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I thought I would give Members a preview of some of these novel concepts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Every year, I will bring something representing the heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This company is called Project Enigma, and they use 3D printing to produce this puzzle and many other puzzles as well as toys to improve people's learning and health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides their retail kiosk in Ang Mo Kio, Project Enigma has started a puzzle museum and library at Henderson Community Club (CC) and it is also running community workshops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, they do not just confine their presence to their shop.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They went out beyond that to the CCs to do events to raise awareness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: My MTI colleagues have placed many of their interesting puzzles and toys in the Members' room because we are keenly aware that after one whole week of Budget and COS debates, Members might want to tinker with this and exercise different parts of your brain muscles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Tea Dojo offers freshly brewed, healthier, syrup-free bubble tea.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I alerted Minister Ong Ye Kung and the Health Promotion Board that I am going to do this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The nutri grade of this oolong tea, the peach oolong tea, is grade A.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, we brought three flavours: peach oolong as well as grape boba, and the third flavour is mango pomelo.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have prepared many of these drinks and after we have the clarification time, we can all have our break soon and Members can choose from any of the three flavours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I have set aside two cups for you in your office and, if you need more, you can let us know.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, this is our freshly brewed, healthier, syrup-free bubble tea made from a specially invented tea machine.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many of our heartland enterprises are coming up with novel concepts, business models and revenue models.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Bukit Gombak Neighbourhood Centre will be turned into a Modern Heritage Heartland Hub or 邻里特色文化基地.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: From 5 to 7 April next month, Bukit Gombak will hold the Rasa Gombak Day Out, a first of its kind festival that will showcase the history and heritage of the popular neighbourhood centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over at the other side of the island, Tampines West Neighbourhood Centre will be transformed into a Heartland Events Hub, or 新兴社区活动站.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last October, Tampines West Merchant Association worked with the Singapore Retailers Association (SRA) to organise Wunderground.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This was a pop-up event featuring collaborations between urban city lifestyle brands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Residents can look forward to more such events in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the past three years, we have ramped up our efforts to transform and to revitalise the heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We supported the Federation of Merchant Associations Singapore (FMAS) and Heartland Enterprise Centre Singapore (HECS) to hold more than 60 placemaking activities all over Singapore in different neighbourhood centres, including the three successful runs of the Heartland Festival.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Collectively, this initiative strengthens each precinct's identity and allows businesses to differentiate their products and also enhance their value proposition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On the ground, we are glad that heartland shops and merchants are stepping up with fresh ideas to co-curate events to make our neighbourhoods more exciting and vibrant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Bold at Work is a co-working space provider and a youth engagement consultant in Jurong East.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They turned parking lots in Yuhua into an interesting space for live music performance, carnival games and workshop.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: That, in turn, drew a lot of people to that whole place, also catalysing demand for the products and services of the heartland shops there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will encourage more creative ways to reach out to audiences and customers in the heartland.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will launch the Heartland Enterprise Placemaking Grant, or 邻里企业社区营造计划, to support our heartland enterprises in creating delightful experiences in the housing estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will make available funding of up to $10,000 for eligible heartland enterprises to organise placemaking projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am sure many good ideas are out there waiting to be explored.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, we want to encourage our heartland enterprises to come forward with exciting proposals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Let us look forward to new possibilities that we can co-curate together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, our SMEs are the backbone of our economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our neighbourhood businesses, besides playing an important role in the economy, also serve as emotional hubs for the community, carrying many of our growing-up memories and enhancing the cohesion of our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Therefore, MTI is committed to supporting our SMEs and neighbourhood businesses, equipping them with the capabilities to address the challenges of the future economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This includes various plans and measures to assist SMEs in their transformation as well as to revitalise neighbourhood businesses, injecting more vitality into these communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over the past three years, we have supported the Federation of Merchants’ Association Singapore and Heartland Enterprise Centre Singapore in organising over 60 neighbourhood placemaking activities, including the annual Heartlands Festival.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through this series of activities, Singaporeans have gained a deeper understanding of the history and unique aspects of each neighbourhood, while neighbourhood businesses have gained confidence in building their brands, using technology to expand their customer base, and even expanding their businesses overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Bee Choo Origin, which expanded from one outlet in Ang Mo Kio to 11 overseas markets, providing the company with new business and development opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition to projects led by the Government, business associations and Chambers of Commerce, our neighbourhoods, businesses have also taken the initiative to organise events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These activities transform the ordinary into the extraordinary, bringing new vitality to the neighbourhood community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through this series of new initiatives and grants, we hope to encourage SMEs, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, and neighbourhood businesses to unleash their creativity, seize the opportunities for economic transformation and drive sustainable development for Singapore. : Chairman, the green transition presents both opportunities and challenges to enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Ms He Ting Ru and Mr Neil Parekh that the Government will continue to deepen and widen our support for businesses through the different stages of their sustainability journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we are enhancing our existing support to help businesses to become more sustainable through the Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In 2022, we launched the EEG to help our enterprises defray rising energy costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since then, Mr Edward Chia and Mr Mark Lee would be glad to know that almost 2,000 companies have used EEG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, CF F&B, a drink stall in a food court.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to give Members examples like that so that you know that EEG is not just used by bigger SMEs but can be used by heartland merchants or even a food stall in a food court.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, CF F&B is a drink stall in a food court.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They used the grant to procure three energy-efficient water heaters that led to cost savings of about 80%, 80% cost savings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will help more businesses invest in energy-efficient equipment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: EEG will be open to other industries, such as maritime, construction and data centres by the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTI is working closely with the industry to onboard additional sectors as necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also streamline the application process by consolidating all the EEG applications from different sectors on the Business Grants Portal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: EEG complements existing schemes like the Enterprise Sustainability Programme (ESP) to provide holistic end-to-end support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, companies can tap into ESP for consultancy support to pinpoint areas for efficiency gains before applying to buy the energy-efficient equipment under EEG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will enable more businesses to tap into the grant for their projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Mr Edward Chia pointed out, data centres and chip manufacturers would do well to use schemes like the EFS (Green) to reduce their emissions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: A company that has benefited from EFS (Green) is Koollogix.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It tapped into this scheme to transform and complete a new lab facility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This, together with other transformation efforts, led to a tenfold increase in their revenue just within two years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Ministry of Finance has announced that climate-related disclosures will be mandated for large companies in Singapore in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Therefore, businesses need capabilities and resources to track and report their carbon footprint.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To this end, we will provide funding support of up to 30% to large companies to kickstart their sustainability reporting journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While smaller companies will not be affected by the new regulations, sustainability reporting will help them to stay relevant as disclosure of carbon footprint data becomes commonplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will complement the pre-scoped carbon accounting solutions offered under the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA) Advanced Digital Solutions Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, to help businesses pursue sustainability-related collaborations while maintaining healthy competition, the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) has developed an Environmental Sustainability Collaboration Guidance Note.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Hence, we are boosting our support for the workforce to upskill and reskill to seize new opportunities in the green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, we set up the Green Skills Committee to develop skills and training programmes aimed at fostering a low-carbon economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, we will continue to build on two focus areas: (a) sustainability reporting; and (b) energy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To develop skills in sustainability reporting, we will provide salary support to sustainability reporting service providers to train interns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, we will launch training programmes for the energy sector to address clean energy skills gaps identified by the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These courses will certainly help workers capture their potential in this growth sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, another emerging area which offers exciting prospects is the digital economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Singapore companies have made good progress in digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many of us will agree that the COVID-19 pandemic has really catalysed the adoption of digital tools and technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many Members spoke during your cuts about AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With the rise of technologies, like Generative AI, digitalisation has become more urgent and dynamic than ever before.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to share more about how we are helping our SMEs to adopt GenAI and I want to assure the Members, Mr Derrick Goh, Mr Keith Chua, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Mr Neil Parekh, that MTI will support businesses in the next lap of enterprise digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage businesses to start exploring and using AI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Interested firms can tap on Enterprise Singapore and IMDA's newly-launched Generative AI Sandbox for SMEs to gain hands-on experience with GenAI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Sandbox will feature affordable and easy-to-use solutions applicable to a broad spectrum of sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I will cite two ways they can use it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, our SMEs can use marketing and sales solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will really them to grow their topline and bottom-line.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They can use GenAI to help them use marketing and sales solutions to generate unique content, such as customised emails and product images for their marketing campaigns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Another area is customer engagement solutions, which can also allow the SMEs to engage customers on a much larger scale better.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These GenAI-powered chatbots can simplify the information search process and then allow businesses to free up their resources and become more productive, so they can allow their staff to focus on higher value-add work, serve customers and maybe allow them to focus on the business development kind of functions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to encourage our SMEs to participate in the Sandbox and get a head start in using GenAI solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, sectoral transformation, the green transition and seizing digital opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many Members talked about the importance of trade associations and chambers (TACs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And indeed, TACs are critical industry multipliers we work with to drive industry transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since 2022, we have supported 30 TACs to spearhead industry initiatives benefitting some 14,000 companies through the Local Enterprise and Association Development Programme (LEAD).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We partnered with TACs to set up SME Centres island-wide to offer SMEs capability development programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, more than 30,000 SMEs benefitted from these services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to reassure Mr Derrick Goh that the SME Centres will continue supporting business transformation efforts, particularly in digitalisation and sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: TACs also represent the interests and needs of the respective industries and form a vital bridge between the industry, the private sector and the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our close partnerships with TACs help us to better understand and address critical concerns on the ground.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Business costs and competitiveness are top-of-mind issues for many SMEs and many businesses today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While there is no magic bullet for these pain points, the private and public sectors and the union representatives have come together to co-create solutions to overcome these challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will form an Alliance for Action (AfA) on Business Competitiveness co-chaired by myself and hon Member Mr Mark Lee, who represents SBF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The AfA will forge solutions with the industry and adopt recommendations to help businesses become more competitive in the long term.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This complements existing efforts by the Pro-Enterprise Panel (PEP) to enhance the regulatory journey for businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To enable TACs to be effective change agents, the Government has invested significantly in developing their capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to work with SBF to boost the capabilities of TACs' secretariats to serve their members better.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: SBF will share more details on this effort in the later part of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We appreciate the close partnership with CASE, and all the work that CASE has done to support consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTI, the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) and the economic agencies will continue to work closely with CASE to protect consumer interests as consumer purchasing habits evolve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, this sustained spirit of collaboration and cooperation between the private sector, public sector and industry associations gives us the grit, give us the resilience to overcome challenging circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our gumption to embrace transformation will set a formidable front against the odds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Let us keep up the momentum of transformation, from reshaping industry, whether it is M&OE or heartland enterprises, energising our heartland shops as well and also seizing potential in digital economy as well as the green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Because by taking shared ownership of our transformation path, we will set sails of positive change and ride new waves of opportunities to reach the harbour of a thriving future for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, we have recovered robustly from the difficult pandemic years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This exceeded EDB's medium-term goals and is partly why Singapore remains Asia's most competitive economy and the world's fourth most competitive, according to the International Institute for Management Development (IMD).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As the world's Global-Asia or Singapore as a hub for cultures, ideas and commerce, how can we strengthen our position as the world's hub?

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, by strengthening our appeal as a vibrant destination for both businesses and tourists alike and residents; and second, by deepening and widening our international partnerships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There has been a resurgence in visitor arrivals and an energetic revival of our city as a bustling hub of eclectic experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have launched new local experiences to capture the winds of recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling was your heartland guide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We opened the Bird Paradise at the Mandai Wildlife Reserve, HyperDrive at Sentosa and Van Gogh: The Immersive Experience at Resorts World Sentosa.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also enjoyed a vibrant calendar of signature events, like the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix or the inaugural edition of ART SG as part of Singapore Art Week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Then, we have live entertainment which resumed with unparalleled vitality, as Singapore played host to prominent acts, such as Blackpink, Ed Sheeran, Jacky Cheung and, of course, a particular act that is currently taking Singapore by storm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our Meetings, Incentives, Conventions and Exhibitions industry, or MICE for short, have also made a very strong comeback.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In 2023, we hosted some of the world's largest MICE events, like Asia Tech x Singapore, Gastech and Herbalife APAC Extravaganza.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also welcomed new events, like the 25th World Congress of Dermatology, which is our largest medical congress to date; and the transport logistic and air cargo for Southeast Asia, with the first in the edition for the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Then, we have also our homegrown events, which many of you have participated in, such as Singapore International Energy Week, our Singapore International Cyber Week, the Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology (SWITCH) and, of course, the Singapore Fintech Festival, which continued year after year to attract a significant turnout.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Conference organisers tell me that they choose Singapore because of our position as a global meeting point for talent, ideas and for business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Even during massive disruptions like COVID-19, Singapore continued to deliver, safely and reliably and these conference organisers are bullish about our prospects to continue to play host to world-class events if there are disruptions in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, confidence in us is strong. through world class events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will develop and market new products and experiences, including supporting local enterprises as they develop new intellectual properties, rejuvenate existing tourism offerings and also upskill our tourism workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are boosting this Fund 4 because it has introduced exciting attractions and lifestyle events here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And I got to launch some of these, including TRIFECTA, which is Asia's first snow, surf and skate lifestyle destination and also, of course, the year-round exclusive homeporting of Disney Cruise Line's latest cruise ship, Disney Adventure, which will start in Singapore next year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Over the past two years, this fund has also helped over 100 local tourism businesses become even more productive and more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, we encourage all of our tourism companies to make full use of the top-up to grow your business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, we are also developing a pipeline of high quality and first-of-its-kind experiences here in Singapore, that we will launch in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will help us to maintain international mindshare and strengthen our appeal as a compelling destination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, we are improving accessibility in Sentosa with Sensoryscape which is a new attraction that will connect Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) and Sentosa's beaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It has multi-sensorial gardens that pique the senses and showcase digital light displays in the night.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Some of us had a sneak peek and we look forward to the soft launch this month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Staying at Sentosa at RWS, I broke ground on Universal Studios, Singapore's Minion Land just two years ago and we look forward to the launch next year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Next year, RWS will also launch the new Singapore Oceanarium which is an expansion of the current SEA Aquarium but three times its size.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As part of RWS' expansion, there will also be a new waterfront lifestyle development and a driverless transport system between the mainland and RWS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Third, we have a strong line-up of leisure and business events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Together with the suite of world-class live entertainment events, we will host high quality MICE events this year, such as the Global Sustainable Tourism Council Global Conference, which is the first in Singapore and NRF 2024: Retail's Big Show Asia Pacific, which is a significant tradeshow for our region’s retail industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Also, when MBS' expansion is completed in the later part of this decade, it will allow us to host more notable live entertainment and MICE events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To continue enhancing Singapore as a vibrant lifestyle and economic hub, we must continue to build our creative economy, as Ms Usha Chandrasdas suggested.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will share how we are doing so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, Singapore hosts many high-quality arts and cultural experiences that enhance our attractiveness as a lively lifestyle hub or lifestyle destination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our year-round arts and cultural calendar features events such as Singapore Art Week and Singapore International Festival of Arts, as well as cultural festivals in Chinatown, Little India and Kampong Gelam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These events which many of you have attended are popular not just with our locals but also our visitors alike, and STB will continue to work with event organisers to improve and grow their appeal and also look for new themes, new arts and cultural experiences which have international appeal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The DesignSingapore Council, which is a subsidiary under EDB, drives the growth of our design sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
